talk_track: Barry Hess here — I spent 16 years as CTO of a DoD small business taking a patented tactical Android platform from the lab to operators in theater. Your live Chief Engineer posting asks for someone who has carried space hardware 'from System Concept, System Requirements to Technology Readiness Level 9' and has 'successfully flown two spacecrafts from concept to mission operations.' Read plainly, that req says the road from your funded prototype to a fielded system is currently unowned — and the search for someone who has flown two birds can run longer than a seed runway. What killed my own platform wasn't the hardware gates; it was force-wide adoption dying for lack of a senior champion inside the customer's building, which is why I now build deployment architecture and acquisition advocacy in parallel from day one. The distance between CDR sign-offs and a program of record is a different discipline than either founder engineering or spacecraft systems review. Who owns your transition plan while the Chief Engineer seat is empty?
